therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: PD-L1 immune checkpoint blockade combined with PARP inhibition
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: Enhanced anti-tumor immune response through checkpoint inhibition while inducing DNA damage repair deficiency via PARP inhibition
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Patients with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Phase 1b: Dose limiting toxicities; Phase 2: Objective response rate per RECIST v1.1

results.target_engagement_evidence: Avelumab steady-state concentrations achieved with geometric mean Cmax ~200 μg/mL and trough ~30-50 μg/mL; Talazoparib steady-state concentrations ~4000-9000 pg/mL
biomarker_changes: CA-125 response in ovarian cancer cohorts: 45.0% (C1) and 63.6% (C2)
PSA response in mCRPC cohorts: 9.5% (E1) and 5.6% (E2)
Low immunogenicity with 6/211 participants developing anti-drug antibodies
subgroup_findings: Highest response rates in BRCA-mutated ovarian cancer (63.6%)
DDR+ breast cancer showed 34.8% response rate
results.dose_information: Avelumab 800 mg Q2W + Talazoparib 1 mg QD (0.75 mg QD for moderate renal impairment)
